This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (North-West) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2631 Bighas and 04 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2004/L&B/LA/28199 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2631 Bighas 04 Biswas land situated in the revenue estate of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi.

The said land is free from all sorts of encumbrances and no litigation in respect of the said land is pending before any court of law, and was being used for agricultural purposes and having many trees which have not been considered while granting compensation.
6.

It is stated that the petitioners have accepted the award amount without prejudice to its rights and has not received the compensation till the filing of the present petition and the petitioners shall accept the award amount under protest.

The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly inadequate and LAC no. 224/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Om Prakash & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 13 insufficient and not in accordance with the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

sentences.text: The petitioners have made appearance before the learned LAC and filed representation and put forth their grievance in writing for enhancement of compensation, however, they were not called for negotiation.

7. As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

The learned LAC has not appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.
The market value of the acquired land is only to be determined by keeping in view the marketability and potentiality of the land".
It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.

(ii) It is stated that the LAC should have taken into the consideration the future potentiality of the land and should have determine the market value by keeping in view the market value as fixed by the Government for allotment of residential flats/plots.

The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.
The ld. LAC has also not considered the status of the said land which is very fertile and levelled and gives 2-3 commercial crops in a year.
The said land hardly needs any development to be done which makes it fit to be used either for industrial or commercial or residential purposes.

(iv) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration that the said land is very close to railway line and metro station, FCI Godown and also surrounded by many developed colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Roop Vihar etc.

The basic amenities are available in an around the said land i.e. water,
electricity, mettaled road, general market, Post Office, transport facilities, banking facilities,
hospitals, schools, colleges, fire station, telephone exchange, railway station, police Station, farm houses and is very near to NH-8, however, the learned LAC has not considered all these factors while passing the said award.

(v) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 06.02.2006, however, physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been taken to the date of payment, therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.

sentences.text: The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the allottees of the residential plot/flats.

The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.

The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.

The DDA and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 5000 per square yards, therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value,
which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after affixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
(vii) It is prayed that the petitioners by way of present petition are claiming market value of the said land @ Rs. 10,000 per square along with interest on solatium and interest @ 24% with effect from the date of the notification under Section 4 of the Act.

sentences.text: It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
11. It is submitted that the possession of the said land has not been taken by DDA.

It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioner is not entitled for grant of enhancement of compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition are denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.
12. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 10.11.2014:-
ISSUES

14. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue-wise findings and determination are as under : -
Whether the petitioner is entitled to the enhancement in compensation, if so, to what extent.
15.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
16.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
